sentences.text: The aforesaid petition was referred to mediation for resolving the disputes between the parties.

In the course of mediation, the petitioner and the respondent along with their counsels were present, the parties identified each other and they resolved their disputes and have agreed to the following terms and conditions:
1. Both the parties state that their marriage was solemnized between the petitioner and the respondent on 01.05.2006 in the residence of the respondent at Mohara Kala Bera Uchada Village, Bewar District, Rajasthan as per Hindu rites and customs.
2. Due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility the parties have been living separately from 2 years.
3. Both the parties

state that they have 3 children born to them from this wedlock by name NIKHIL KUMAWATH, aged about 18 years and NIKHITHA KUMAWATH aged about 16 years and NELLU KUMAWATH aged about 15 years, taking the children welfare and future as the paramount interest both the parties herein undertakes not to persue this petition.
4.
The parties further state that there has been no collusion or force, fraud or any undue influence in entering into this compromise in the aforesaid manner.
5. Both the parties herein state that, they have arrived at this agreement without pressing on the allegations leveled against each other orally or expressly in view of this agreement.

6. In view of this agreement the respondent agreed and undertakes to quash/close in C.C.2900/2024 filed against the petitioner and others, pending before 31st ACJM.,
Bengaluru filed u/s.498A, 506, 504 and 354 of IPC.
III. In view of the aforesaid agreement entered into between the parties, the petitioner and the respondent pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to dispose off as not to press this case.
NC: 2026:KHC:12123 HC-KAR IV.
The parties will appear on 16.12.2025 before the Hon'ble Court for passing orders in terms of the agreement."

5. Therefore, in light of the settlement arrived at by the parties as quoted supra and the offences not being against the State, I deem it appropriate to terminate the proceedings pending against these petitioners in the subject petitions.

6. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER i.
Criminal Petitions are disposed.
